verses.eng: She continues her repentance. "'9. Have mercy upon me, O Light, for they have oppressed me again. Because of your commandment, the light in me is distracted and my power and my understanding. "'10. My power has begun to wane whiles I am in these afflictions, and the number of my time whiles I am in the chaos. My light is diminished, for they have taken away my power from me, and all the powers in me are tossed about. "'11. I am become powerless in the presence of all the rulers of the aeons, who hate me, and in the presence of the four-and-twenty emanations, in whose region I was. And my brother, my

pair, was afraid to help me, because of that in which they have set me. "'12. And all the rulers of the height have counted me as matter in which is no light. I am become as a material power which has fallen out of the rulers, "'13. And all who are in the aeons said: She has become chaos. And thereafter all the pitiless powers encompassed me together and proposed to take away the whole light in me. "'14. But I have trusted in you, O Light, and said: You are my saviour. "'15. And my commandment, which you have decreed for me, is in your hands. Save me out of the hands of the emanations of Self-willed, which oppress me and persecute me. "'16. Send your light over me, for I am as naught before you, and save me according to your compassion. "'17. Let me not be despised, for I have sung praises to you, O Light. Let chaos cover the emanations of Self-willed, let them be led down into the darkness. "'18. Let the mouth of them be shut up, who would devour me with guile, who say: Let us take the whole light in her,--although I have done them no ill.'"

And when Jesus had spoken this, Mathathayahaw came forward and said: "My Adanay, your spirit has stirred me and your light has made me sober to proclaim this eighth repentance of Pistis Sophia. For your power has prophesied thereof aforetime through Dawad in the thirtieth Psalm, saying:
Mathathayahaw interprets the eighth repentance from Psalm xxx. "'1. On you, O Adanay, have I hoped. Let

me never be put to shame; save me according to your righteousness. "'2. Incline your ear to me, save me quickly. Be you to me a protecting God and a house of refuge to save me. "'3. For you are my support and my refuge; for your name's sake you will guide me and feed me. "'4. And you will draw me out of this snare, which they have laid privily for me; for you are my protection. "'5. Into your hands I will render my spirit; you have redeemed me, O Adanay, God of Truth. "'6. You have hated them who hold to vain emptiness; but I have trusted. "'7. And I shall rejoice because of my Adanay and make merry over your grace. For you have looked down upon my humbleness and saved my soul out of my necessities. "'8. And you have not shut me up in the hands of my foes; you have set my feet on a broad space. "'9. Be gracious to me, O Adanay, for I am afflicted; my eye is distracted in the wrath and my soul and my body. "'10. For my years have wasted away in sadness and my life is wasted in sighing. My power is enfeebled in misery and my bones are distracted. "'11. I am become a mockery for all my foes and my neighbours. I am become a fright for my acquaintances, and they who saw me, are fled away from me. "'12. I am forgotten in their heart as a corpse, and I have become as a ruined vessel. "'13. For I have heard the scorn of many who

encompass me round about. Massing themselves together against me, they took counsel to take away my soul from me. "'14. But I have trusted in you, O Adanay. I said: You are my God. "'15. My lots are in your hands. Save me from the hand of my foes and free me from my persecutors. "'16. Reveal your face over your slave, and free me according to your grace, O Adanay. "'17. Let me not be put to shame, for I have cried to, you. Let the impious be put to shame and turn towards hell. "'18. Let the crafty lips be struck dumb, which allege iniquity against the righteous in pride and scorn.'"

Jesus commends Mathathayahaw and promises his disciples that they shall sit on thrones with him. And when Jesus had heard these words, he said: "Finely said], Mathathayahaw. Now, therefore, amen, I say to you: When the perfect number is completed and the universe is raised hence, I will take my seat in the Treasury of the Light, and you yourselves will sit on twelve light-powers, until we have restored all the orders of the twelve saviours to the region of the inheritances of every one of them."
And when he had said this, he said: stand you what I say?"

Marayam interprets the words of Jesus. Marayam came forward and said: "O Adanay, concerning this matter you have said to us aforetime in similitude: 'You have awaited with me in the trials, and I will bequeath to you a kingdom, as my Father has bequeathed it to me, that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom; and you shall sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.'"

Jesus continued again and said to his disciples: "It came to pass then thereafter, when the emanations of Self-willed oppressed Pistis Sophia in the chaos, that she uttered the ninth repentance, saying:

The ninth repentance of Sophia. "'1. O Light, smite down them who have taken away my power from me, and take away the power from them who have taken away mine from me. "'2. For I am your power and your light. Come and save me. "'3. Let great darkness cover my oppressors. Say to my power: I am he who will save you. "'4. Let all those who would take away my light from me utterly, lack their power. Let them face about to the chaos and become powerless, who would take away my light from me utterly. "'5. Let their power be as dust, and let Yew, your angel, smite them. "'6. And if they would go into the height, let darkness seize upon them and let them slip down and turn to the chaos. And let your angel Yew pursue them and cast them down into the darkness below. "'7. For they have set a lion-faced power as a trap for me, although I have done them no ill, from which its light will be taken; and they have oppressed the power in me, which they will not be able to take away. "'8. Now, therefore, O Light, take away the purification from the lion-faced power without its knowing it,--the thought which Self-willed has

thought, to take away my light; take away his own and let the light be taken away from the lion-faced power, which set the trap for me. "'9. But my power will exult in the Light and rejoice that he will save it. "'10. And all the portions of my power shall say: There is no saviour but you. For you will save me out of the hand of the lion-faced power, which has taken away my power from me, and you save me out of the hands of them who have taken away my power and my light from me. "'11. For they have risen up against me, lying against me and saying that I know the mystery of the Light which is in the height, [the Light] in which I have had faith. And they have constrained me, saying:] Tell to us the mystery of the Light in the height,--that which I know not. "'12. And they have requited me with all this ill because I have had faith in the Light of the height; and they have made my power lightless. "'13. But when they constrained me, I sat in the darkness, my soul bowed down in mourning. "'14. And do you, O Light--for that reason sing I praise to you--save me. I know that you will save me because I fulfilled your will ever since I was in my aeon. I fulfilled your will, as the invisibles who are in my region, and as my pair. And I mourned, looking unceasingly and searching for the Light. "'15. Now, therefore, have all the emanations of Self-willed surrounded me and rejoiced over me and sore oppressed me without my knowing

[them]. And they have fled away and ceased from me but have had no pity upon me. "'16. They have returned again and made trial of me and they have oppressed me in great oppression and ground their teeth against me, desiring to take away my light from me utterly. "'17. How long, therefore, O Light, do you suffer them, that they oppress me? Save my power from their evil thoughts and save me from the hand of the lion-faced power; for I alone of the invisibles am in this region. "'18. I will sing praises to you, O Light, in the midst of all who are gathered together against me, and I will cry to you in the midst of all who oppress me. "'19. Now, therefore, O Light, let not them who hate me and desire to take away my power from me, rejoice over me--who hate me and flash their eyes against me, though I have not done anything to them. "'20. For indeed they have fawned upon me with sweet words, asking me concerning the mysteries of the Light which I know not, and have craftily spoken against me and been enraged against me, because I have had faith in the Light in the height. "'21. They have opened their chops against me and said.: Well indeed, we will take from her her light. "'22. Now, therefore, O Light, you have known their guile; suffer them not and let not your help be far from me. "'23. Quickly, O Light, vindicate and avenge me,

to your goodness. Now, therefore, O Light of lights, let them not take away my light from me, "'25. And let them not say in their heart: Our power is glutted with her light. And let them not say: We have consumed her power. "'26. But rather let darkness come upon them, and let those who long to take away my light from me, become powerless, and let them be clothed with chaos and darkness, who say there: We will take away her light and her power. "'27. Now, therefore, save me that I may rejoice, for I long for the thirteenth aeon, the region of Righteousness, and I shall say ever-more: May the light of your angel Yew shine more and more. "'28. And my tongue will sing praises to you in your gnosis my whole time in the thirteenth aeon.'
It came to pass, when Jesus had finished saying these words to his disciples, that he said to them: "Who is sober among you, let him proclaim their solution."

Yaiqab came forward, kissed the breast of Jesus and said: "My Adanay, your spirit has sobered me, and I am ready to proclaim their solution. Concerning them indeed your power has prophesied aforetime through Dawad in the thirty-fourth Psalm, saying thus concerning the ninth repentance of Pistis Sophia:

Yaiqab interprets the ninth repentance from Psalm xxxiv. "'1. Give sentence, O Adanay, on them who do me injustice, and fight against them who fight against me. "'2. Lay hand on weapon and shield and stand up to help me. "'3. Draw forth a sword and conceal it [ sic ] from my oppressors. Say to my soul: I am your salvation. "'4. Let them be put to shame and abashed who strive after my soul; let them fall back and be put to shame who imagine evil against me. "'5. Let them be as chaff before the wind, and let the angel of the Adanay pursue after them. "'6. Let their way be darkness and slippery, and let the angel of the Adanay oppress them. "'7. For without cause have they hid a snare for me for their own spoiling, and they have mocked at my soul in vain. "'8. Let a snare come upon them which they know not, and let the net which they have hid for me, catch them, and let them fall into this snare. "'9. But my soul will exult in the Adanay and rejoice in its salvation. "'10. All my bones shall say: O Adanay, who can be like to you?--you who set free the wretched from the hand of him who is stronger than him; and you save a wretched and poor one] from the hands of them who spoil him. "11. Unjust witnesses came forward and have asked me that which I knew not. "'12. They have requited me evil for good and childlessness for my soul. "13. But when they molested me, I clothed me in a sack and humbled my soul with fasting, and my prayer will return into my breast. "'14. I was pleasing to you, as to my neighbour and as to my brother; and I

humbled myself as one in mourning and as one who is sad. "'15. They have rejoiced over me, and they are put to shame. Scourges have gathered themselves together against me and I knew not; they were cut off and were troubled. "'16. They have brought me to trial and mocked me with mocking; they have ground their teeth against me. "'17. O Adanay, when will you look upon me? Restore again my soul from their evil works and save my only one from the hands of the lions. "'18. I will confess to you, O Adanay, in the great assembly, and I will sing praises to you in the midst of a countless people. "'19. Let not them who unjustly treat me as a foe, rejoice over me, who hate me without a cause and wink with their eyes. "'20. For indeed they discourse with me with words of peace, though they plot wrath with craft. "'21. They opened their chops wide against me and said: Well indeed, our eyes have filled our sight with him. "'22. You have seen, O Adanay. Keep not silence, O Adanay, withdraw not yourself from me. "'23. Arise, O Adanay, and give heed to my vindication, give heed to my vengeance, my God and my Adanay. "'24. Judge me, O Adanay, according to your justice; let them not rejoice over me, my God. "'25. And let them not say: Well done, our soul. Let them not say: We have consumed him. "'26. Let them be put to shame and be scorned, who rejoice at my mischance. Let

them be clothed with shame and disgrace who speak boastingly against me. "'27. Let them who desire my justification, exult and rejoice and let them who desire the peace of his slave, say: May the Adanay be great and arise. "'28. My tongue will exult over your justification and over your honour all the day long.'" Next: Chapter 52

Jesus commends Yaiqab and promises the first place to the disciples. When Yaiqab then had said this, Jesus said to him: Well said, finely, Yaiqab. This is the solution of the ninth repentance of Pistis Sophia. Aman, amen, I say to you: You shall be the first in the kingdom of heaven before all invisibles and all gods and rulers who are in the thirteenth aeon and in the twelfth aeon; and not only you, but also every one who shall accomplish my mysteries."
And when he had said this, he said to them: Understand you in what manner I discourse with you?"

Marayam interprets the words of Jesus. Marayam started forward again and said: "Yea, O Adanay, this is what you did say to us aforetime: 'The last shall be first and the first shall be last.' The first then, who were created before us, are the invisibles, for indeed they arose before mankind, they and the gods and the rulers; and the men who shall receive mysteries, will be first into the kingdom of heaven."

The repentance of Sophia is accepted. Jesus is sent to help her. Jesus continued again and said to his disciples: "It came to pass then, when Pistis Sophia had proclaimed the ninth repentance, that the lion-faced power oppressed her again, desiring to take away all powers from her. She cried out again to the Light, saying: "'O Light, in whom I have had faith from the beginning, for whose sake I have endured these great pains, help me.'

"And in that hour her repentance was accepted from her. The First Mystery hearkened to her, and I was sent off at his command. I came to help her, and led her up out of the chaos, because she had repented, and also because she had had faith in the Light and had endured these great pains and these great perils. She had been deluded through the god-like Self-willed, and had not been deluded through anything else, save through an light-power, because of its resemblance to the Light in which she had had faith. For this cause then was I sent forth at the command of the First Mystery to help her secretly. I did not however yet go to the region of the aeons at all; but I passed down through the midst out of them, without any single power knowing it, either those of the interior of the interior or those of the exterior of the exterior, save only the First Mystery.

"It came to pass then, when I came into the chaos to help her, that she saw me, that I was understanding and shone exceedingly and was full of compassion for her. For I was not self-willed as the lion-faced power, which had taken away the light-power from Sophia, and had also oppressed her in order to take away from her the whole light in her. Sophia then saw me, that I shone thousand times more than the lion-faced power, and that I was full of compassion for her. And she knew that I came out of the Height of heights, in whose light she had had faith from the beginning. Pistis Sophia then
took courage and uttered the tenth repentance, saying:

The tenth repentance of Sophia. "'1. I have cried to you, O Light of lights, in my oppression and you have hearkened to me. "'2. O Light, save my power from unjust and lawless lips and from crafty traps. "'3. The light which was being taken from me in crafty snaring, will not be brought to you. "'4. For the traps of Self-willed and the nooses of the merciless one] are spread out. "'5. Woe to me, that my dwelling was far off, and I was in the dwellings of the chaos. "'6. My power was in regions which are not mine. "'7. And I entreated those merciless ones]; and when I entreated them, they fought against me without a cause.'"
When then Jesus had said this to his disciples, he said to them: "Now, therefore, let him whom his spirit stirs, come forward and speak the solution of the tenth repentance of Pistis Sophia."
Kayapaa answered and said: "O Adanay, concerning this your light-power prophesied aforetime through Dawad in the one-hundred-and-nineteenth Psalm; saying:

Kayapaa interprets the tenth repentance from Psalm cxix. "'1. I cried to you, O Adanay, in my oppression, and you hearken to me. "'2. O Adanay, save my soul from unjust lips and from crafty tongues. "'3. What will be given to you or what will be added to you with a crafty tongue? "'4. The arrows of the strong one] are made sharp with the coal of the desert. "'5. Woe to me, that my dwelling is far off, and I dwelt in the tents of Qadar. "'6. My soul has dwelt in many regions as a guest. "'7. I was peaceful with them who hate peace; if I spoke to them, they fought against me without a cause.'
Jesus commends Kayapaa. Jesus said to him: Well said, Kayapaa, and finely. This is the solution of the tenth repentance of Pistis Sophia."
"'1. Dan has the mighty power raised itself in evil?

The eleventh repentance of Sophia. "'2. Its plotting takes away the light from me all the time, and as sharp iron have they taken away power from me. "'3. I chose to descend into the chaos rather than to abide in the thirteenth aeon, the region of Righteousness. "'4. And they desired to lead me craftily, in order to consume my whole light. "'5. For this cause then will the Light take

away their whole light, and also their whole matter will be made naught. And it will take away their light and not suffer them to abide in the thirteenth aeon, their dwelling-place, and will not have their name in the region of those who shall live. "'6. And the four-and-twenty emanations will see what has befallen you, O lion-faced power, and will be afraid and not be disobedient, but give the purification of their light.
"Now, therefore, let him in whom his power is raised, come forward and proclaim the solution of the eleventh repentance of Pistis Sophia."
Then Salome came forward and said: "My Adanay, concerning this your light-power prophesied aforetime through Dawad in the fifty-first Psalm, saying:

Salome interprets the repentance from Psalm li. "'1. Dan does the mighty one] boast himself in his wickedness? "'2. Your tongue has studied unrighteousness all the day long; as a sharp razor have you practised craft. "'3. You lovedst wickedness more than goodness; you lovedst to speak unrighteousness more than righteousness. "'4. You lovedst all words of submerging and a crafty tongue. "'5. Wherefor will God bring you to naught

utterly, and will uproot you and drag you out from your dwelling-place, and will root out your root and cast it away from the livingSelah. "'6. The righteous will see and be afraid, and they will mock at him and say: "'7. Lo, an man who made not God for his helper, but trusted to his great riches and was mighty in his vanity. "'8. But I am as a fruit-bearing olive-tree in the house of God. I have trusted in the grace of God from all eternity. "'9. And I will confess to you, for you have dealt faithfully with me; and I will wait on your name, for it is auspicious in the presence of your holy ones].'
"This then is now, therefore, my Adanay, the solution of the eleventh repentance of Pistis Sophia. While your light-power has roused me, I have spoken it according to your desire."

Jesus commends Salome. It came to pass then, when Jesus had heard these words which Salome spoke, that he said: Well said, Salome. Aman, amen, I say to you: I will perfect you in all mysteries of the kingdom of the Light."
